name: Gharat
description: Gharat is an Iranian fishing-loot game where players match ranks to steal cards from the central play pile or from the top of opponents' capture piles.

overview.description: Gharat is an Iranian fishing-loot game where players match ranks to steal cards from the central play pile or from the top of opponents' capture piles.

history.origins: Gharat was documented in Iran as a fishing game whose name means loot, reflecting rank-match theft from visible pile tops.
timeline: Traditional era: Played as a local Iranian rank-matching capture game.
Modern era: Documented in international rule collections and English-language card-game references.
history.cultural: The game emphasizes hidden stack memory and tactical stealing from opponents.
history.evolution: Core rules remained stable; some tables add a pair-play convenience variant.

setup.players: 2, 3, or 4 players, with optional partnerships at 4.
setup.dealing: Start play pile with four face-up stacked cards (only top visible), deal four cards to each player, and keep remainder as face-down stock for future 4-card redeals.
setup.equipment: Score sheet for cumulative target race.

rules.objective: Capture high-value cards and reach agreed cumulative target score before opponents.
rules.gameplay: Play begins with player to dealer's right and proceeds counterclockwise. On turn, play exactly one card from hand. If its rank matches the top of any table pile (central play pile or any capture pile), take that top card plus any immediately underlying equal-rank cards and place them on top of your capture pile. If no match exists, place played card on top of central play pile. After all players exhaust current 4-card hands, dealer gives another 4 to each if stock remains. Continue until stock and hands are empty.
keyRules: Only top cards of piles are visible and inspectable; hidden underlying cards are unknown until uncovered.
Suits are irrelevant; rank only matters for matching.
A player may effectively steal from their own capture pile by matching its top rank.
Uncaptured cards left in play pile at end score for nobody.

strategy.basic: Avoid feeding obvious top-rank matches to opponents when you cannot immediately reclaim them.
strategy.intermediate: Track likely hidden runs under pile tops to predict high-value future captures.
strategy.advanced: Control top-rank exposure timing so opponents reveal useful buried cards that you can steal next turn.
tips: Ace captures are especially valuable and worth protecting from immediate theft.
In team play, coordinate top-rank setup rather than competing for the same pile.

variations.name: Pair Play Easy Variant
variations.description: A player holding a pair may place both to capture pile in one turn, then skips later turn(s) to compensate card count.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Pair-play variant only changes turn count; no engine constants or config overrides are documented in sources.

scoring.description: Number cards score 5 each, J/Q/K score 10 each, and Aces score 20 each from captured piles only.
scoring.winCondition: First player or team to reach or exceed agreed target total, usually 500 or 1000, wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: Iranian fishing game where matching top ranks can steal cards from center or opponents' capture piles.

hero.title: GHARAT
hero.subtitle: Iranian Loot Fishing
hero.tagline: Match top ranks, steal stacks, and race to the target.
